problem:
Which of the following geometric series converge?

- $-1+1-1+1-⋯$
- $\frac{4}{3}-1+\frac{3}{4}-\frac{9}{16}+⋯$
- $0.1+0.11+0.121+0.133\,1+⋯$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following geometric series converge?

- $1+5+25+125+⋯$
- $\frac{2}{7}+\frac{4}{3}+\frac{56}{9}+\frac{784}{27}+⋯$
- $0.1+0.01+0.001+0.000\,1+⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's look at each series in turn.

- For the geometric series $1+5+25+125+⋯$ the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} & =\frac{5}{1} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r|\ge 1.$

- For the geometric series $\frac{2}{7}+\frac{4}{3}+\frac{56}{9}+\frac{784}{27}+⋯$ the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} & =\frac{(\frac{4}{3})}{(\frac{2}{7})} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{7}{2} \\  & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r|\ge 1.$

- For the geometric series $0.1+0.01+0.001+0.000\,1+⋯$  the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} & =\frac{0.01}{0.1} \\  & =0.1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is convergent because $|r|<1.$

In conclusion, only series III converges.
